items.name: server is PostgreSQL 17.6; a fresh database has NO default ACLs (pg_default_acl empty)
MAINTAIN exists and is part of ALL TABLES on 17: GRANT ALL gives the 'm' bit and has_table_privilege(...,'MAINTAIN') is true; GRANT SELECT does not
a new function has NULL proacl and PUBLIC (hence anon) may EXECUTE it: the implicit default that Supabase leaves anon with

ACL ENTRY ORDER is not canonical: revoking ALL from a role and granting it back MOVES its aclitem to the END of relacl::text, so two catalogs with the same grants can have different relacl::text (F3's fingerprints hash relacl::text); sorted entries are equal
a plain re-GRANT of a privilege the role already has does NOT reorder (the reorder needs the entry to be removed first)
functions behave the same: after REVOKE ALL FROM the roles + GRANT in a different order than the original (the shape of F3's rollback), proacl::text changes but its sorted entries do not

NEGATIVE CONTROL (this assertion FAILS under the OLD expression): hashing relacl::text / attacl::text / proacl::text gives a DIFFERENT fingerprint for the same privileges after revoke + re-grant moved the anon entry to the end (relation, column and function ACLs)
the R1 sorted-aclitem expression gives the SAME fingerprint before and after the reorder, for relation, column and function ACLs (the assertion the old expression fails)

the sorted expression is still SENSITIVE: a real privilege change (extra INSERT for anon; a dropped function grant; a column grant removed) changes the fingerprint, and NULL (default ACL) stays distinct from an empty '{}' ACL

every R1 APPLY/ROLLBACK pack variant (16 files: #91 APPLY-1/1B/2 + ROLLBACK-1/1B/2, #92 APPLY-92/ROLLBACK-92, 10A APPLY-1C/APPLY-92-44col/ROLLBACK-1C/ROLLBACK-2-after-1C, F3 FORWARD/ROLLBACK, 11A install/rollback; the F3 DRIFT_QUERY and POSTCHECKS read-only files are excluded) has ONE top-level BEGIN followed IMMEDIATELY (comments aside) by exactly: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'; then pg_advisory_xact_lock(KEY); then SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'; the same KEY in all of them, and no statement before BEGIN (R1 + lock_timeout follow-up: the timeout is set before the lock so it bounds the lock wait itself, and again after it)

TWO REAL CONNECTIONS, WITH the lock: B (same lock text as every pack) blocks on the advisory lock while A is mid-transaction (pg_locks: ungranted advisory lock, key = the pack key) and B's first statement runs only AFTER A committed (B.start >= A.end; no overlap)
NEGATIVE CONTROL (two real connections, lock statement REMOVED): B does NOT wait; its first statement runs INSIDE A's open transaction (B.start < A.end) = the overlap the lock prevents
the lock is released by ABORT too: A fails (division by zero) while holding the lock; B (blocked meanwhile) then proceeds and commits; nothing of A remains

TIMEOUT (two real connections, the exact lock text of every pack): A holds the pack lock ~7 s; B (blocked on the advisory lock, pg_locks shows it ungranted) fails with SQLSTATE 55P03 lock_not_available after ~5 s (4.5-6.5 s), NOT after A's ~7 s and not never; A is unaffected (commits, both its probe rows present); B left no row; the lock is free afterwards

NEGATIVE CONTROL for LK.5 (what the literal 'timeout only AFTER the lock' placement would do): with the pre-lock SET LOCAL lock_timeout REMOVED (the lock followed by the timeout) B is NOT bounded: it waits out A's whole ~7 s hold (> 5 s) and then succeeds; this is why the timeout is also set BEFORE the lock

TIMEOUT on a REAL pack (R1 APPLY-1, first run held ~7 s before COMMIT): the second APPLY-1 fails with 55P03 after ~5 s, took no public-table lock and changed nothing of its own; the first run commits normally and the catalog equals exactly ONE APPLY-1

CROSS-PACK on the replica: the R1 F3 forward (A, held ~2 s) and the R1 11A install (B, a different pack) share the key, so B waits on the advisory lock until F3 commits; both then succeed and the end state has the F3 guard row AND can_upload_event_media
